name: Hazael
overview: Hazael was a male king over Aram, as noted in 1 Kings 19:15. While his tribal affiliation is not recorded, he is recognized primarily for his royal leadership over the Aramean people. No additional personal notes are provided beyond his kingship.
namesAndTitles: The name Hazael means 'G-d [El] sees,' reflecting a theologically rich Hebrew name. His title, King of Aram, straightforwardly identifies his political role and authority over the Aramean kingdom, as referenced in 2 Kings 8:28.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that Ben-hadad was Hazael's father, according to 2 Kings 13:3. Beyond this, no other family relationships are explicitly recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hazael is significant in the biblical narrative as the king of Aram, a major regional power during the time of the divided kingdoms of Israel and Judah. His reign marks an important period of interaction and conflict with Israel, underscoring God's providence and sovereignty over nations. The meaning of his name also subtly points to God's watchful oversight even over foreign rulers.
